raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

JIT kernel wrappers that launch through tvm-ffi enter `torch.cuda.device(t.device)` around the launch. Entering and leaving it costs about 1.6 µs per call on an x86 host, even when `t` is already on the current device, which is always the case in a one-device-per-process server. The qknorm complex RoPE wrappers used by Qwen-Image-2.1 run it on every attention layer.

## Modifications

- `sglang.kernels.jit.utils.device_guard(t)` returns a shared `nullcontext` when `t.get_device()` is the current device, and `torch.cuda.device(t.device)` otherwise.
- `qknorm_complex_rope_cuda` and `qknorm_complex_rope_pack_` use it.

Behaviour on another device is unchanged. Other wrappers can adopt the helper one line at a time.

## Accuracy Tests

On 2xH200:
- `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_device_guard.py`: 2 passed. With the tensor on the current device, `torch.cuda.device` is never constructed (it is monkeypatched to raise). With a tensor on `cuda:1`, the device is entered and restored.
- `test_complex_rope.py`: 38 passed.
- `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: 25 passed.
- `test_model_fast_paths.py`: 114 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base `c15edf314d`, H200 (Xeon 8558P).

| | µs per call |
|---|---|
| `torch.cuda.device(t.device)` enter and exit | 1.64 |
| `device_guard(t)`, current device | 0.49 |

End to end the change is too small to resolve on H200. In Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2 512², with both paths in one server and chosen per request, it measured +0.27% (faster in 5/16) against an in-process A/A of 0.00%: the wrapper runs about 2,400 times per request. The saving is per call. Grace hosts pay roughly twice the x86 Python cost.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""``device_guard`` enters a tensor's CUDA device only when it is not the current one."""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import device_guard
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=5, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+
+def test_current_device_enters_no_guard(monkeypatch):
+    x = torch.empty(1, device=f"cuda:{torch.cuda.current_device()}")
+
+    def entered(device):
+        raise AssertionError(f"guard entered for {device}")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "device", entered)
+    with device_guard(x):
+        assert torch.cuda.current_device() == x.get_device()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(torch.cuda.device_count() < 2, reason="needs two GPUs")
+def test_other_device_is_entered_and_restored():
+    torch.cuda.set_device(0)
+    x = torch.empty(1, device="cuda:1")
+    with device_guard(x):
+        assert torch.cuda.current_device() == 1
+    assert torch.cuda.current_device() == 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
